title: The mysterious
hookLine: Einstein wrote that the most beautiful thing we can experience is the mysterious

cards: What's the most beautiful thing a person can experience? Ask around and the answers come quickly. A newborn's face.
A sunrise over water. Falling in love. A piece of music that stops you halfway up the stairs.
Albert Einstein, the physicist, gave a different answer in an essay about what he believed: the most beautiful thing we can experience is the mysterious. Not the solved. The mysterious.

teach.b: His words are paraphrased here, not quoted. First, the claim. The most beautiful thing we can experience, Einstein wrote, is the mysterious.
Not a puzzle waiting for an answer key, but something real we can sense and can't get to the bottom of. Second, where it leads.

teach.h: THE SOURCE OF ART AND SCIENCE
teach.b: He called it the source of all true art and all true science. That's a surprise from a scientist. Plenty of people picture science as a machine for getting rid of mystery.
He says the opposite: mystery is where the work begins, and where it keeps coming from. Third, what happens without it.
A person to whom this feeling is a stranger, Einstein wrote, who can no longer pause to wonder and stand rapt in awe, is as good as dead: their eyes are closed. Strong words. Fourth, his religion.
Knowing that something we can't penetrate exists, a deep reason and a radiant beauty our minds can grasp only in their most basic forms, is at the heart of true religiousness, he went on.
Then he drew a careful line: in that sense, and in that sense only, he counted himself among the devoutly religious.
He was naming his own meaning of the word, not setting a rule for anyone else's.

how: Some people on a personal spiritual path, religious and not, keep a practice of sitting with an open question rather than an answer, and Einstein's essay is often read as a description of that kind of wonder.

o: what Einstein called the most beautiful thing we can experience
what Einstein called the last problem science will one day solve
Einstein's name for the parts of physics he could not finish

games.q: Einstein on the mysterious — tap the pairs.
p: the most beautiful thing we can experience
as good as dead, eyes closed

s: Einstein wrote that mystery is the enemy of science
he called the mysterious the source of all true art and all true science.
Einstein wrote that someone who can no longer wonder is as good as dead
he said their eyes are closed.
Einstein said he was religious in every sense of the word
he said in this sense, and in this sense only.

games.q: someone asks Einstein whether he counts himself religious. how does his essay answer?
o: yes, in the ordinary sense of the word.
only in the sense of awe before what we can't penetrate.
games.why: he wrote that in that sense, and in that sense only, he counted himself among the devoutly religious.

practice: Choose one thing you can't explain and probably never will: why music can move someone to tears, what another person's inner life is really like, why the world can be understood at all.
Hold it the way you'd hold a stone in your palm, without trying to solve it. When the mind starts arguing, set the argument down and go back to simply holding the question.

wordCard.voice: The mysterious. Einstein's name for what we sense but can't get to the bottom of, which he called the most beautiful thing we can experience. Today's word.

orig.note: German, from Einstein's essay: the most beautiful thing … the mysterious.

carryVoice: Your line: stand rapt in awe. Not the solved, the mysterious. Back tomorrow, same hill.
